title: Resolve the dead ParentId-null guard in HasParentCycle
description:
Source: docs/tasks/tickets/CC-080-has-parent-cycle-dead-null-guard.md
Source key: CC-080
Source status: Backlog
Source priority: P3

## Summary

`HasParentCycle` contains `if (current.ParentId == null) break;`. Under schema v2
`ParentId` is always set (the validator rejects null at a separate site), so the
guard never fires for valid definitions. It only matters if a legacy or
hand-built definition deserializes with a null ParentId.

## Scope

- Decide whether the guard is dead under v2 and remove it (with a test proving
  no v2 definition reaches it), or keep it and document it as a defensive guard
  for legacy data.
- Do not change the cycle-detection result in either case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The decision is recorded on the ticket.
- If removed, a regression test asserts cycle detection still works and a legacy
  null-ParentId definition is handled without an infinite loop.

## Validation

- Runtime definition tests for cycle detection with and without null ParentId.

## Findings

Raised as finding 2.5 in the 2026-08-24 audit addendum. The guard is defensive
rather than harmful; the cleanup value is documenting the intent or removing the
dead branch.

## Blockers

None.

## Next Step

Remove or comment the guard, then run the definition cycle tests.

comments.body:
## Sprint Round 3 (TSK-0084) — decision + validation evidence

**Decision:** Chose scope option (b) — KEEP the null-`ParentId` guard in `CreaturePartHierarchyIndex.HasParentCycle` and document it as a deliberate defensive guard for legacy/hand-built v1-style data. Rationale: under schema v2 a valid definition always sets `ParentId` (DefinitionValidator rejects null at `ValidateParentsAndCycles`), so the null branch is only reachable from legacy/hand-built data; removing it would not change cycle-detection results for valid definitions, and keeping it guarantees the parent walk terminates without an infinite loop for such data. The guard was NOT removed; it is now self-documenting via an explanatory comment (CC-080 finding 2.5). `BodyId` remains the explicit v2 root sentinel.

**Changed files (worktree):**
- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Definition/CreaturePartHierarchyIndex.cs`: added a detailed comment explaining the defensive null-`ParentId` root-termination branch in `HasParentCycle`. No logic change — cycle-detection result unchanged (acceptance criterion 2 satisfied by construction).
- `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/CreatureDefinitionTests.cs`: added two regression tests —
  1. `HasParentCycle_NullParentLegacyRootIsNotACycleAndDoesNotMaskSiblingCycle`: a legacy null-`ParentId` root is not reported as a cycle, and does not mask a genuine sibling self-cycle (terminates; a hang would fail the run).
  2. `HasParentCycle_AllNullParentLegacyRoots_IsNotACycle`: an all-null-parent legacy forest returns false and terminates.

**Validation (independently run):**
- dotnet build --no-restore: `ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj` and `ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj` both 0 warnings / 0 errors.
- Unity PlayMode full Runtime suite (`ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime`): **519/519 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** — includes both new TSK-0084 tests.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Confirmed `CreatureDefinition.HasParentCycle` delegates to `CreaturePartHierarchyIndex.HasParentCycle`, so the tests exercise the documented guard.
